steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) on September 30, 2026, while ET is EDT (UTC-4) until early November. So Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET.

**ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).**

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is on PET (UTC−5) year-round, so subtract 5 hours from UTC.

That makes **July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC** equal to **July 15, 2026, 07:00** in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST is UTC+2, and Tokyo is JST (UTC+9), so Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Time in October 2026 if daylight saving has ended? Actually, on October 11, 2026, Madrid is still on CEST (UTC+2), since DST in Europe typically ends later in October. PDT is UTC-7, so the deadline is 9 hours ahead in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST on March 3, 2026 is 9 hours behind Madrid time in March? Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) on March 3, while PST is UTC−8, so Madrid is 9 hours ahead.

So the deadline is on the next day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On February 2, 2026, CET is UTC+1, and Los Angeles is on PST (UTC−8), so the deadline is 9 hours earlier locally.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is 14 hours ahead of Lima time (Peru is UTC−5, JST is UTC+9). So 8:00 AM on May 5, 2026 in JST is 6:00 PM on May 4, 2026 in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Time in late October, while PT on October 28, 2026 is Pacific Daylight Time (UTC−7).  
11:59 PM PT on October 28, 2026 corresponds to 8:59 AM in Madrid on October 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is typically 6 hours ahead of Eastern Time on October 30, 2026, so 9:00 AM ET would be 3:00 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 15:00 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

New York is on Eastern Time. On October 27, 2026, New York will still be on daylight saving time (EDT, UTC−4), while CET is UTC+1, so New York is 5 hours behind CET.

So, 18:00 CET on October 27, 2026 is 13:00 in New York.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT is November 3, 2026 at 08:59 in Madrid, Spain (CET).

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on CET on March 20, 2026, which is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time (PT, UTC−7) because PT is on daylight saving time then. So 11:59 PM PT on March 20, 2026 is 8:59 AM in Madrid on March 21, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles on March 25, 2026, so 12:00 PM CET is 3:00 AM in Los Angeles.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 03:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Eastern Time on October 12, 2026 is either EDT or EST depending on daylight saving time; on that date, ET is still on daylight time (EDT, UTC−4) until early November.  
So 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026 is 6:00 AM in Madrid on October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE means “Anywhere on Earth,” which is UTC−12. So the deadline is October 10, 2026 at 11:59 in Madrid local time if Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) then.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 11:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide is on ACDT (UTC+10:30) on October 6, 2026. Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) then. So Adelaide is 8 hours 30 minutes ahead of Madrid.
